test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - Numerical Ability (Held on: 23 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: An item was sold at a profit of 23.75%. If the cost price of the item was Rs. 1,000 more than what it actually was, while the selling price remained unchanged, the profit earned would have been only 10%. What was the actual cost price of the item (in Rs.)?
solution:
**Given:**

Let the actual cost price be ₹x.

Profit percentage = 23.75%

New cost price = ₹(x + 1000)

New profit percentage = 10%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (S.P.) = C.P. times (1 + dfrac{{Profit %}}{100}) 

**Calculation:**

Selling Price with actual cost price:

 S.P. = x times (1 + dfrac{23.75}{100}) 

⇒ S.P. = x times dfrac{123.75}{100} 

New Selling Price with increased cost price:

 S.P. = (x + 1000) times (1 + dfrac{10}{100}) 

⇒ S.P. = (x + 1000) times dfrac{110}{100} 

Since the selling price remains the same:

 x times dfrac{123.75}{100} = (x + 1000) times dfrac{110}{100} 

⇒ 123.75x = 110x + 110000 

⇒ 13.75x = 11000 

⇒ x = dfrac{11000}{13.75} 

⇒ x = 800 

∴ The actual cost price of the item is ₹800.

4a:T
